summary.plain: In 1979 the MARK J experiment at DESY's PETRA collider analysed how the energy of e+e- collisions is spread out. It defined a quantity called oblateness and reported three-jet structure seen unambiguously for the first time, as expected if a quark radiates a gluon.
summary.technical: MARK-J analysis of the spatial energy distribution of e⁺e⁻ → hadrons at PETRA: the 'oblateness' variable describes the flat shape of the energy configuration; the data show three-jet structure, 'unambiguously observed for the first time', explained by QCD predictions for quark-antiquark production with hard non-collinear gluons (Phys. Rev. Lett. 43, 830, 17 September 1979).

title: Discovery of Three-Jet Events and a Test of Quantum Chromodynamics at PETRA
why_it_matters: The abstract states that the data can be explained by quantum chromodynamic predictions for quark-antiquark pairs accompanied by hard noncollinear gluons.
